core_obligations: The transported embedding (proof lines 7596-7599): given a functorial injective embedding A to (A -> J(A)) on the source category, the author defines for an object B of the target category the map from B into the value of the right adjoint at J(vB).

Functoriality and injectivity (proof lines 7599-7601): the assignment is functorial in B by functoriality of v and J, and each map is an injection into an injective object by the same argument as in the preceding lemma, so the target category has functorial injective embeddings.
proof_roadmap: Take the given functorial injective embedding on the source.
Define the candidate embedding on the target by composing with the adjoint transpose.
Note functoriality and invoke the preceding argument for injectivity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that under the hypotheses of the preceding lemma together with the existence of functorial injective embeddings in the source category, the target category also has functorial injective embeddings (statement lines 7580-7594). The proof is a complete argument: the given functorial embedding of the source is transported across the adjunction by sending an object to the value of the right adjoint at the embedding of its image (proof lines 7596-7599), and the resulting assignment is functorial by functoriality of the three ingredients while injectivity follows exactly as in the preceding lemma (proof lines 7599-7601). The non-formal content is the construction of the transported embedding. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
